title: Flickbar
description: Snap, resize and move macOS windows with trackpad gestures on their title bars. Free and open source.
heroLede: Swipe two fingers on a title bar to snap a Mac window to a half, a third or a quarter, fill the screen or send it to another display.
heroMeta:
Free and open source
macOS 14 or later
tryText: Pick one below to see what it does.
featuresTitle: Arrange windows without reaching for the keyboard
featuresIntro: Your hand is already on the trackpad. Flickbar turns the title bar into a place to gesture, and leaves the rest of your scrolling alone.
f1Title: Every common layout is one swipe
f1Text1: Swipe left or right for a half, then keep swiping the same way for two thirds and one third. Swipe up to fill the screen, and down to minimize.
f1Text2: While your fingers are down, a highlight glides to where the window will land and a light haptic tap confirms it. Press Esc before lifting to cancel.
f1Alt: Gestures settings, listing what each swipe does
f2Title: A grid for everything in between
f2Text: Rest two fingers on a title bar for a moment and a grid appears: three columns, each full height or split into a top and bottom half. Slide to a cell and lift to snap there.
f3Text: Swipe up on an app’s Dock icon to show all of its windows, down to hide it, sideways to bring its next window forward, or pinch in to quit it. On a minimized window’s tile, any title-bar gesture brings it back and snaps it.
f4Text: After you grant access, a practice window walks you through the main gestures and ticks each one off as you do it. Open it again any time from the menu.
f4Alt: The gesture tutorial, with the first three steps ticked
f5Text1: Choose what each gesture does, give any action a keyboard shortcut, add space between snapped windows, and turn gestures off in apps that need their title bars to themselves.
f5Text2: Hold ⌥ Option to gesture anywhere in a window, or ⌘ to send it to the display on that side. Flickbar speaks English, French and Persian.
f5Alt: General settings: spacing between windows, preview, haptics, language, open at login and updates
gesturesIntro: Put the pointer on a window’s title bar or a Dock icon and use two fingers. Each of these can be remapped in Settings.
tSideResult: Left or right half; repeat for ⅔, then ⅓
tQuarter: Swipe sideways, then up or down
tUpResult: Fill the screen; repeat for the middle third
tDownResult: Minimize (or restore the size from before snapping, if you choose)
tCommandResult: Move to the display on that side
tHoldResult: Pick a layout from the grid
dUpResult: Show all of the app’s windows
dSideResult: Bring the app’s next window to the front
shortcutsNote: Every action can also have a keyboard shortcut. None are set at first, so Flickbar never takes over keys you already use.
fact1Text: No analytics, no account. Update checks are off until you turn them on, and they send only Flickbar’s version number.
fact2Text: Releases are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, and updates install only if they match Flickbar’s own signing key.
fact3Text: Made by Parsa Kamalipour and licensed under the GPL. Read the code, build it yourself, or send a pull request.
a1: Yes. There’s no trial, paid tier or account. Flickbar is free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later license.
q2: Why does it ask for Accessibility access?
a2: macOS requires it for any app that moves or resizes other apps’ windows. Flickbar uses it only to find the window or Dock icon under the pointer and act on it when you gesture or press a shortcut.
q3: Will it get in the way of normal scrolling?
a3: No. Only two-finger gestures that start on a title bar or Dock icon are used. All other scrolling and zooming passes through untouched, and mouse wheels are ignored.
a4: For gestures, yes. Keyboard shortcuts work with any keyboard, so you can use Flickbar with a mouse too.
a5: Turn on Zoom in or out and Smart zoom in System Settings → Trackpad → Scroll & Zoom. macOS only sends those gestures when they’re enabled.
a6: English, French and Persian. Flickbar follows your Mac’s language, or choose one in Settings → General → Language.
q7: How do I update or uninstall it?
a7: Choose Check for Updates… from Flickbar’s menu, or turn on daily checks in Settings. With Homebrew you can also run brew upgrade --cask flickbar. To uninstall, quit Flickbar from its menu bar icon and move it to the Trash, or run brew uninstall --cask flickbar.
endTitle: Give your title bars something to do
endText: Free, open source and ready in a minute.
